stages.ask: Why is one side of a dune steeper?

explain.say: Dunes form where there is lots of loose sand and a strong wind, in deserts and on beaches. A small obstacle like a bush or rock slows the wind, and sand starts to pile up behind it.

explain.say: At the top, the wind slows and drops the grains. When the pile gets too steep, sand avalanches down the far side, making a steep slope called the slip face.

explain.say: Grain by grain, sand is taken from the back and dropped on the front, so the whole dune creeps downwind, sometimes many metres a year.

faq.a: Wind lifts sand grains a little way, and they bounce along the ground in hops called saltation. Each landing grain knocks others into the air. Bigger grains roll and slide.

faq.q: Why is one side of a dune steeper?
faq.a: Wind pushes sand up the gentle side and drops it just past the top. The sand piles up until it slides down in small avalanches, making a steep slip face at about 30 to 34 degrees.
Yes. Sand is blown from the back of the dune to the front, so the dune slowly travels downwind, often several metres a year, and can bury roads and buildings.

faq.q: How tall can sand dunes get?
faq.a: The tallest dunes are hundreds of metres high. Some star dunes in deserts like the Badain Jaran in China and in Namibia reach about 300 to 500 metres.
asks: What is the biggest sand dune?

faq.q: Are most deserts covered in sand dunes?
faq.a: No. Only about a fifth of the world's deserts are sandy. Most are bare rock, gravel and stony plains.

facts: The slip face of a dune usually stands at about 30 to 34 degrees, the steepest angle loose sand can hold.
Only about 20 percent of the Earth's deserts are covered by sand.
